messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: GPU pool 'inference-primary' saturation detected — queue depth spike and failed autoscale attempts. recent 5m token ingress +420% vs baseline. attempting automated mitigation but hit scale cap. paging olivia (oncall)

olivia: I'm on it. seeing elevated 429 and 504 rates on hosted endpoints, correlation with high queue depth. linking trace: https://internal.traces/r/inf-pool/2182104321

sre-bot: autoscaler logs show repeated ScaleUpError: 'quota-exceeded' and then backoff. last successful scale was 12m ago. continuous-batcher metrics also show throughput drop ~30%.

raj: joining. what's the active rollout? any recent config changes to batching or cache?

maria: Heads up — we promoted a runtime config canary 30m ago that tweaks continuous_batching.max_window from 80ms -> 25ms and prefix_cache.ttl from 5m -> 30s to reduce memory pressure for the new quantized kernels. can confirm the change landed to 30% of pods via rollout flag.

kevin: that TTL and window drop would definitely increase cold-prefix misses and reduce effective batching. fewer tokens bundled -> higher per-token compute -> GPU saturation. also autoscaler sees more pods hitting high cpu/gpu simultaneously causing scale thrash.

olivia: confirming customer impact: support reports 429s for embeddings route from enterprise-customer-alpha and increased tail latency for chat for several startups. alex, can you pull a short customer impact summary?

alex: I pulled logs — enterprise-customer-alpha (eu-west) saw 47% request failures in the past 15m, avg latency for chat generation jumped 2.3x. Support has a flag on the account and is sending notices.

raj: immediate plan: 1) stop rollout (pause/roll back canary), 2) manually scale the pool up + add a temporary burst node group, 3) revert continuous_batching.max_window and prefix_cache.ttl to previous values, 4) monitor for queue drain and 429 reduction. assigning tasks.

maria: I can revert the runtime flag. command to revert: 
```
kubectl patch config runtime-config -n inference -p '{"spec":{"continuous_batching.max_window":80,"prefix_cache.ttl":"5m"}}'
```
I'll apply to the canary and then promote if stable. doing canary rollback now.

kevin: I'll open a manual scale. CLI: 
```
infractl pool scale inference-primary --add-nodes 8 --instance-type a100-80gb --reason "incident 2182104321 manual burst"
```
Executing now. expected nodes available ~90s.

sre-bot: autoscaler reported 'scale cap reached' at 2182104260. manual scale request accepted, new nodes provisioning.

olivia: Maria — after you revert, can you also bump prefix_cache.max_prefetch=4? we want more aggressive prefetching to avoid cold spiral.

maria: ack. applying prefetch bump after TTL revert. patch applied to canary.

kevin: new nodes healthy and joined cluster. pool capacity +8 confirmed. queue depth down 18% in the last 45s.

raj: seeing 429 rate falling from 18% -> 6% for chat endpoints. embeddings still elevated but trending down. keep a 5 min cadence on metrics.

olivia: oncall handoff — I'm staying on until we hit <1% 429 and latency back to normal. if anything regresses escalate to infra lead. Raj, can you prepare rollback PR and postmortem draft?

raj: will do. opening PR for the runtime-config rollback and a rollback guard to prevent future auto-promotes when pool utilization > 65%. PR link: https://git.internal/r/rc/12345

alex: sent customer update to enterprise-customer-alpha and a PSR to affected customers noting transient throttling and that we've applied mitigations.

maria: canary rollback confirmed. continuous_batching.max_window restored to 80ms, prefix_cache.ttl restored to 5m, max_prefetch set to 4. changes propagated to 100% canary within 2m.

sre-bot: metrics snapshot at 2182104610: queue depth -45% vs peak, gpu-util falling from 98% -> 72%, 429 rate 3.2%, 500 rate 0.6%.

kevin: recommend leaving the manual burst running for 30m while we validate and then scale down gradually — autoscaler still has weird hysteresis due to prior thrash, don't remove capacity abruptly. I'll annotate the infra runbook.

olivia: agreed. keep burst for 30m. Raj — start postmortem template and include timeline, root cause hypothesis: config regression (aggressive batching window + low prefix ttl) -> prefix-cache cold spiral -> reduced batching efficiency -> per-token compute increase -> pool saturation -> autoscaler hit scale cap + thrash. Also include mitigation steps and the customer impact log.

raj: drafting. items for follow-up: 1) add pre-deploy smoke for 'small-batch perf' that compares throughput and cache-hit rates, 2) make rollout safety check: block runtime config pushes if pool_util > 60%, 3) alert on sudden prefix_cache.hit_rate drop (>20% within 10m), 4) update runbook to include manual-burst commands and rollback PR checklist.

maria: adding an automated canary gate that runs a micro-benchmark with embedding+chat workload before promotion. will open PR for that.

olivia: thanks team. I'll stay online until metrics stable and will do a handoff 30m. if anyone sees a regression ping me. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: incident declared resolved->monitoring when last_message_ts >= 2182104687 and 429 rate < 1% sustained for 15m. please update incident tracker: https://incidents.internal/2182104321

raj: noted, will update tracker and attach logs. postmortem ETA EOD.

kevin: scaling down burst in 28m unless otherwise flagged. leaving a note in infra-runbook.

alex: customers updated. support queue has a high-priority tag on any related follow-ups.

olivia: handoff summary for next oncall: root cause probable config regression in runtime canary changing continuous batching and prefix cache TTL; mitigation: rollback runtime flags, manual burst scale-up, bump prefetch; customer impact: transient 429s and latency spikes affecting multiple customers, enterprise-alpha most impacted. next steps: postmortem + gating + alerts. I'm logging off after metrics stable.

sre-bot: incident status: mitigated -> monitoring.
